evidence.excerpt:
Memory for large language model (LLM) agents has rapidly evolved
from simple retrieval-augmented mechanisms into a data manage-
ment system that supports persistent information storage, retrieval,
update, consolidation, and dynamic lifecycle governance through-
out agent execution. Despite this evolution, existing evaluations
still benchmark agent memory mainly through end-to-end task suc-
cess metrics (e.g., F1, BLEU), while treating the underlying system
as a monolithic black box. As a result, critical system-level concerns,
including operational costs, architectural trade-offs across mem-
ory modules, and robustness under dynamic knowledge updates,
remain insufficiently explored.
In this paper, we present a systematic experimental study of
agent memory from a data management perspective. We propose
an analytical framework that decomposes agent memory into four
core modules: memory

trieval and routing, and maintenance. Under this framework, we
evaluate 12 representative memory systems and two reference base-
lines across five benchmark workloads spanning 11 datasets. Our
extensive end-to-end evaluation shows that no single architecture
dominates across all scenarios; instead, effectiveness depends heav-
ily on how well the memory structure aligns with the workload

quantify their individual effects on representation fidelity, retrieval
precision, update correctness, and long-horizon stability. Finally, we

nization. Based on these findings, we identify promising directions
towards building truly agent-native memory

mental modules. By systematically generating controlled variants
that modify one module at a time, we evaluate the contribution of
each module to overall system performance.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline findings are measured with external benchmark ground truths and deterministic metrics such as Exact Match, ROUGE-L, Recall@K, DB-Bench task success, and recorded latency traces, which are not the signals used to design the evaluated systems.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Established benchmark ground truths and deterministic metrics, including Exact Match, Answer F1, ROUGE-L, Recall@K, DB-Bench task success, and recorded operation latency.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Pre-existing design choices and heuristics of the 12 evaluated memory systems, such as extraction schemas, retrieval fusion rules, and maintenance policies.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding the absence of a universally dominant memory architecture and the performance-cost trade-offs of localized versus global maintenance are well supported by experimental metrics and fine-grained ablations.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluations span 11 datasets across benchmarks such as LoCoMo, LongMemEval, DB-Bench, and LongBench, utilizing rigorous controlled ablations to isolate the effects of representation formats, extraction granularity, retrieval fusion, and maintenance strategies.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations rely on established external benchmark ground truths and deterministic algorithmic metrics (Exact Match, ROUGE-L, Recall@K, DB-Bench execution success, and measured execution runtime).
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard multi-dimensional task benchmarks (Exact Match, Answer F1, ROUGE-L, Recall@K, DB-Bench Task Success, and operational latency traces).
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Pre-existing designs and heuristics implemented by the 12 evaluated memory systems (e.g., prompt templates, clustering algorithms, vector indexing, and pipeline routing rules).

primary.limitations: The study is an empirical evaluation of existing open architectures rather than introducing a single novel memory model, and operational cost analyses rely on amortized latency traces rather than exhaustive production deployment settings.
primary.method_assessment: The manuscript establishes a clear data-management taxonomy across four functional memory modules and empirically assesses systems on standardized testbeds measuring end-to-end task effectiveness, retrieval fidelity, update robustness, long-horizon stability, and operational latency.
primary.quality_rationale: The study provides thorough, systematic empirical evidence across multiple competitive baselines and varied tasks, adhering to solid experimental controls and offering valuable architectural insights for agent-native memory systems.
primary.scoped_contribution: A comprehensive empirical benchmark and architectural taxonomy analyzing 12 representative agent memory systems and baselines across five workloads, decomposing memory into representation/storage, extraction, retrieval/routing, and maintenance.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study provides thorough, systematic empirical evidence across multiple competitive baselines and varied tasks, adhering to solid experimental controls and offering valuable architectural insights for agent-native memory systems.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The study is an empirical evaluation of existing open architectures rather than introducing a single novel memory model, and operational cost analyses rely on amortized latency traces rather than exhaustive production deployment settings.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
